classification.difficultyReason: Use a common angle and altitude right angles to prove the specified similarity, then obtain the stated ratio from corresponding sides and from the supplied area expressions.

content.prompt: Let $ABC$ be a triangle, and let $BP$ and $CQ$ be altitudes.

spec.description: Unshaded triangle with A above B and C; P is on AC and Q is on AB. The two interior altitudes cross. Ordinary source blue linework is reconstructed in house black.
spec.mathematics: BP is perpendicular to AC at P; CQ is perpendicular to AB at Q. Feet and right-angle markers are derived from the triangle coordinates.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied vertices, altitudes and right-angle markers are visible; no similarity or ratio answers are shown.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Prove that $\triangle ABP$ is similar to $\triangle ACQ$.

answer.short: $\angle BAP=\angle CAQ$ (common angle) and $\angle APB=\angle AQC=90^\circ$. Therefore $\triangle ABP\sim\triangle ACQ$ (AAA).
answer.worked:
In triangles $ABP$ and $ACQ$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle BAP&=\angle CAQ &&\text{(common angle at }A\text{)}\\\angle APB&=\angle AQC=90^\circ &&\text{(altitudes)}\end{align*}$$
Therefore $\triangle ABP\sim\triangle ACQ$ (AAA), with vertices in matching order.

answer.short: $\dfrac{BP}{CQ}=\dfrac{AB}{AC}$, since these are ratios of matching sides of the similar triangles.
answer.worked:
From $\triangle ABP\sim\triangle ACQ$, side $BP$ corresponds to $CQ$, and side $AB$ corresponds to $AC$. Matching sides have equal ratios, so
$$\frac{BP}{CQ}=\frac{AB}{AC}.$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: As an alternative approach, explain why $\dfrac12\times AC\times BP$ and $\dfrac12\times AB\times CQ$ are both equal to the area of $\triangle ABC$.

answer.short: Each is $\tfrac12\times\text{base}\times\text{perpendicular height}$ for the same triangle: $AC$ pairs with $BP$, and $AB$ pairs with $CQ$.
answer.worked:
Using base $AC$, the perpendicular height is $BP$, so the area of $\triangle ABC$ is $\tfrac12\times AC\times BP$.

Using base $AB$, the perpendicular height is $CQ$, so the same area is $\tfrac12\times AB\times CQ$.

answer.short: Equating the two area expressions gives $AC\times BP=AB\times CQ$, hence $\dfrac{BP}{CQ}=\dfrac{AB}{AC}$.
answer.worked:
The two expressions represent the area of the same triangle:
$$\begin{align*}\frac12\times AC\times BP&=\frac12\times AB\times CQ\\AC\times BP&=AB\times CQ\\\frac{BP}{CQ}&=\frac{AB}{AC}.\end{align*}$$
The final line follows by dividing both sides by $AC\times CQ$.
